display.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the Ten Wedding Gifts, Part 2
display.summary_short: Before Shavuos: we were all at Har Sinai, and how to keep tzitzis kosher. Then a lost boy in a blizzard leads to the Baal Shem Tov's ten wedding gifts coming true.
display.summary_long: Before finishing the story, the storyteller prepares listeners for Shavuos. The Rebbe asked that everyone, even babies, come to shul to hear the Ten Commandments, since the Midrash says it is like receiving the Torah anew. Every soul was at Har Sinai, and the Arizal teaches that our generation, the one that will greet Moshiach, are the souls of those who left Mitzrayim. He then explains when a torn tzitzis string makes tzitzis unfit, tells of a young boy who pinned his tzitzis on with a safety pin, and adds the Frierdiker Rebbe's teaching on tzitzis and payos. The story resumes: months after the wedding, on a night of a fierce blizzard, a shivering ten-year-old knocks on Avraham and Sarah's door. They warm him, feed him and bring him home the next morning. He is the only son of a rich poritz, who throws a banquet in their honor, and one nobleman after another gives them the very gifts the Baal Shem Tov's students promised. Just as the tzaddik's words came true, the storyteller says, so will the Rebbe's words about Moshiach. A Yiddish Shavuos song closes the program.
display.lesson: Trust the words of a tzaddik: they will come true, just as the Rebbe's promise of Moshiach will. Help others without looking for a reward.
